component.name: Groundhog
component.summary: Private messaging that keeps its head down

description.p: Groundhog is a GTK4 and libadwaita app for private Nostr messaging. It is a preview: it sends and receives NIP-17 private messages with one person or a small group of up to ten, takes part in relay groups (NIP-29) and Marmot encrypted groups, and keeps messages only on this device, in encrypted storage.

ul.li: Private messages are end-to-end encrypted and sent only to the relays each person chose for receiving them. Your key stays outside Groundhog: use local Grotto or a NIP-46 remote signer on a phone or bunker. Grotto is needed only for Grotto-backed accounts.

Messages, drafts, mutes and blocks are kept in an encrypted database whose key is in your keyring. There is no backup or export: another device can download your private messages again with your key from relays that still hold them.
People you haven’t accepted go to Message Requests, with no profile lookups. You can mute, block, forget a conversation on this device, and mark a person’s key as verified.
Disappearing messages: each conversation can have its own timer, and the composer shows it before you send. Relays are asked to delete expired messages, but may not.
There are no read receipts, typing indicators or online status. Nothing loads from the web unless you ask, and notifications are off by default and hide the sender and text.
Setup can publish the list of relays where people can reach you. No relay is contacted until you choose one.

Relay groups: join a group from its address or invite link, or start one on a relay you choose, then read and send there. A relay group is not end-to-end encrypted: the relay’s operators can read every message and see who wrote it. The group’s relay is contacted only when you choose Join or Create.

Encrypted groups are verified with White Noise Android 2026.9.30 (MDK/MarmotKit 0.11) in the newer format; MDK 0.8-era apps use an older-format group. Some intermediate Marmot app versions cannot join either format, and other versions are not guaranteed to work. Apps limited to different formats cannot share a group. Members can see each other.

description.p: Encrypted attachments in private messages: a photo or file is encrypted on your device and stored on a Blossom server you choose (there is no default), with location and camera data removed from JPEG and PNG photos. A received file is downloaded only when you choose Download, and a decrypted copy is kept only in the encrypted database until you save it somewhere yourself. The server sees the encrypted file's size, when it is uploaded and downloaded, and your IP address unless you use Tor.

To receive encrypted-group invitations, your account publishes two public KeyPackage events by default: one for the adopted Marmot format and one for the older format. Anyone can link both events to each other and to your account. You can turn off older-format invitations in Preferences, but a relay may retain copies of the older event and its public deletion request.

In encrypted groups, relays see ciphertext, timing, sizes and the group relays, not message contents. Group history has no export or restore on another device. Leaving may be local until an admin removes you, so other members may still count you. Encrypted-group attachments go to a Blossom server chosen by you or the group's policy; that server learns your IP address and the encrypted blob's size unless you use Tor.

Not in this version: files in relay groups, and how far along an upload or download is (Groundhog shows only that it is under way). Groundhog can connect through Tor, and then connects to nothing if Tor can't be reached; relays then see Tor instead of your IP address, but still see your account. Otherwise connections go directly to relays, which see your IP address.

Remote signing uses signer relays, which see timing, your IP address unless Tor is enabled, and the link between client and signer transport keys. Remote accounts require encrypted storage: cached messages remain readable while the signer is offline, but new decryptions and signing wait for it. Before downgrading to an alpha without remote signers, select a Grotto-backed account or read-only mode.

Groundhog does not protect against malware running as you, hide that you use Nostr or which relays you use, hide from your own message relays that you receive messages and when, or guarantee that relays or other people delete disappearing messages.
First alpha. Encrypted groups are available by default; the signer app that keeps your key is now called Grotto.

ul.li: Create, join and message encrypted groups with compatible apps. Verified: White Noise Android 2026.9.30 (MDK/MarmotKit 0.11) in the newer format; MDK 0.8-era apps through an older-format group. Some intermediate Marmot app versions cannot join either format, and other versions are not guaranteed to work. Apps limited to different formats cannot share a group.

Your account publishes two linkable KeyPackage events by default, one per format. Group members see each other; relays see ciphertext, timing and group relays. Group history cannot be exported or restored on another device, and leaving may be local until an admin removes you.
Encrypted-group attachments are stored on a Blossom server chosen by you or the group policy; that server learns your IP address and encrypted blob size unless you use Tor.
Loading a long conversation or group history no longer silently skips messages when more than 200 arrive at once

Send and receive photos and files in private conversations: they are encrypted before upload to the file server you choose, location and camera data are removed from photos, and nothing is downloaded until you ask
Pin conversations, mark them read or unread, and a conversation menu in the header
Messages that arrive while Groundhog is closed are notified when it starts, without replaying old history
A note in the conversation when its disappearing timer changes; conversations started by others no longer inherit your default timer
More reliable unread counts and delivery status for group messages
Safer attachment downloads: addresses on your own network, including IPv6 forms that hide one and names that resolve to one, are refused before any connection
Relays can no longer link separate connections through resumed encrypted sessions, in any network mode
Private messages to a small group of up to ten people: each person gets their own separately encrypted copy, sent only to the relays they chose, and delivery is shown per person

Groundwork for encrypted attachments: received photos and files are recognised and shown as such, nothing is downloaded, and the decrypted copy of a file, once downloading arrives, is deleted with its message
A version of Groundhog built without Tor support no longer connects directly when Tor is the chosen network setting: it connects to nothing and says so until you choose another setting

Relay groups (NIP-29): join from an address or invite link, start a group on a relay you choose, read and send, see members and roles, and leave. Relay groups are not end-to-end encrypted, and Groundhog says so.
Connect through Tor: every relay and web lookup goes through Tor, with nothing sent directly if Tor can’t be reached, and connections kept apart so relays can’t link them
Blocked Conversations in Preferences, a context menu on conversations, Ctrl+I for Conversation Info, and contact names as conversation titles
Start a conversation with New Message: paste an npub, or look up a name@domain address only when you choose to
Message Requests: messages from people you haven’t accepted wait apart, with Accept, Delete and Block
Conversation Info: privacy summary, mute, block, forget, disappearing timer, and safety codes to verify each other’s keys
A timer indicator in the composer when messages will disappear
More reliable delivery checks for a contact’s message relays
Send private messages (NIP-17) through a queue that survives restarts, with honest status: waiting for approval, sending, sent to at least one of each person’s relays, or not sent
Encrypted message storage on this device, with history, drafts and retention (keep forever, 1 year or 30 days)
Disappearing messages
Private notifications, off by default
First-run setup of your message relays
